    Home/Menopause

    Menopause treatments, compared with what clinics sell.

    Peptide Chooser editorial team. Checked 30 Oct 2026.

    Every claim links to its source.

    No peptide is FDA approved for menopause symptoms, and none on our lists is sold for them. The FDA-approved options are estradiol, alone or with progesterone, and one non-hormonal pill, fezolinetant (Veozah).

    Compare the options

    Is it legal today?

    For hot flashes and other menopause symptoms: the FDA-approved medicines, and what compounded hormones are.

    • Compounded hormones · pharmacy-made hormones from online clinicsNot FDA approved; pharmacy-madeon prescription

      Hormones made by a pharmacy and sold by some online clinics, not FDA approved.

      Hormones a pharmacy makes itself. The FDA does not verify their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold. 1

      Not FDA approved; pharmacy-made.

      Prescription through the clinic.

      On prescription; no clinic prices yet
    • Estradiol (pill, patch or gel) · estrogen pill, patch or gel for hot flashesFDA approvedon prescription

      An estrogen taken as a pill, patch or gel, FDA approved for hot flashes due to menopause.

      Replaces estrogen, which falls at menopause. In a woman with a uterus, estrogen alone raises the risk of endometrial cancer. 2, 3, 4

      FDA approved for moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause.

      Prescription, from an online clinic or your doctor.

      On prescription; no clinic prices yet
    • Estradiol with progesterone (Bijuva) · one capsule with both hormonesFDA approvedon prescription

      One capsule with both hormones, FDA approved for hot flashes in women with a uterus.

      One capsule each evening with food, with an estrogen and progesterone in it. For women with a uterus. 5

      FDA approved for moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause, in women with a uterus.

      Prescription, from an online clinic or your doctor.

      On prescription; no clinic prices yet
    • Fezolinetant (Veozah) · non-hormonal daily pill for hot flashesFDA approvedon prescription

      A daily non-hormonal pill, FDA approved for hot flashes due to menopause.

      One pill a day with no hormone in it. Its label warns of liver injury, so it needs liver blood tests before and during treatment. 6

      FDA approved for moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause.

      Prescription, with liver blood tests before and during treatment.

      On prescription; no clinic prices yet

    Is it legal today?

    FDA status checked 5 Nov 2026

    Compounded hormones are made by pharmacies and are not FDA approved, so the FDA does not verify their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

    FDA status of the medicines on this page, each with its source.

    MedicineStatusWhat that means
    Compounded hormonesNot FDA approved; pharmacy-mademade by a pharmacy; the FDA does not verify safety, effectiveness or quality before sale 1
    Estradiol (pill, patch or gel)FDA approvedmoderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause, prescription 2
    Estradiol with progesterone (Bijuva)FDA approvedmoderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause, in women with a uterus, prescription 5
    Fezolinetant (Veozah)FDA approvedmoderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause, prescription, with liver blood tests 6

    Approved means the FDA approved a product containing it for a stated use. Compounded means a pharmacy made it; a compounded drug is not FDA approved, even when an approved product has the same ingredient. All substances
